plan.about: The audit plan the F1 Finance Audit Machine follows for the subsequent events review and going concern evaluation of the invented HANGS Construction Services LLC, fiscal year 2026. The runner reads its rates, dates and thresholds from here; the Subsequent Events Files system shows it. Every name and figure is invented.
plan.engagement: FY2026 Subsequent Events and Going Concern
plan.period: Fiscal year ended June 30, 2026; events from July 1 to October 22, 2026
plan.reader: The shareholders, the bonding company and Cinderbrook Bank read the year-end statements; the bank's covenants read them too.

materiality.why: The same materiality serves every FY2026 audit area of HCS. The engagement partner sets the final amounts.

standards.title: Subsequent Events and Subsequently Discovered Facts
standards.how: The auditor performs procedures to identify events between the date of the financial statements and the report date that need adjustment or disclosure: management's procedures, inquiry, the minutes, the latest interim statements, the lawyers' letter. An event that gives more evidence about a condition that existed at the balance sheet date is recognized; one about a condition that arose later is disclosed if leaving it out would mislead. Paraphrased.

standards.title: The Auditor's Consideration of an Entity's Ability to Continue as a Going Concern
standards.how: The auditor evaluates whether conditions and events, considered in the aggregate, raise substantial doubt about the entity's ability to continue for a reasonable period, one year after the statements are available to be issued under ASC 205-40; if they do, the auditor evaluates whether management's plans are probable of being effectively implemented and would alleviate the doubt, and then the disclosure and the report. Paraphrased.

standards.title: Subsequent events; going concern
standards.how: A nonpublic entity discloses the date through which subsequent events were evaluated. When substantial doubt is raised and alleviated by management's plans, the notes describe the conditions, management's evaluation of them and the plans that alleviate the doubt.

assertions.how: The minutes, management's answers, the lawyers' letter, the cash received and paid after the year end and the September 30 books read for anything after June 30
Each event classified: a condition that existed at June 30 is recognized at June 30; one that arose later is disclosed
Each recognized event measured from its document: the settlement, the district's decision, the signed change order
The draft notes compared with every disclosed event, the date through which events were evaluated and the going concern wording
The line of credit's maturity, the covenant headroom at June 30 and September 30, the cash forecast with and without the renewal, and the bank's commitment weighed

procedures.what: Agree the September 30 books' June 30 column to the FY2026 trial balance, propose materiality and set the review period and the going concern look-forward.
Read every meeting of the board of directors, management's written answers and the lawyers' letter with its settlement and fee statement.
Read every receipt and payment after June 30 and the bank's loan and dividend activity for what they say about June 30.
Classify every event as recognized or disclosed, measure each recognized one, and compare the draft notes with what must be disclosed.
Compute the covenants at June 30 and September 30 as the loan agreement defines them, recompute the cash forecast with and without the renewal, and weigh the bank's commitment.
Set what was found against materiality, draft the going concern wording for the CPA, list the open items and write the workpapers and the draft findings memo. The CPA concludes.

folderName: HANGS Construction Services - FY2026 Subsequent Events Files

items: June results reviewed: FY2026 closes with net income of about $1.1 million before the audit.
Pier 9 Tech Center: the owner signed change order CO-07 on July 15 at $240,000.00, not the $610,000.00 HCS priced. The board accepts the signed amount.
Kestrel Point Hotel: credit memo CM-0627 for $28,600.00 issued July 8, as agreed with the owner on June 18.
Brindlewood School District: the district is withholding $41,250.00 of liquidated damages. HCS asked on July 20 for a 12-day time extension.
Corliss Medical Group: still no payment on the $186,935.00 final billing. Resolved: Pellham & Quist to file suit to foreclose the lien.
Line of credit: the $1,200,000.00 advance of August 14 to pay Pier 9 subcontractors while two owner payments were late is ratified.
Pier 9 Tech Center: the owner signed change order CO-08 on August 20 for $570,000.00, courtyard paving and drainage added by the owner.

Tideflats Cold Storage: the panel supplier’s 9% price notice of August 3 and the cracking found in 14 tilt-up panels on August 11. Resolved: recast the panels and claim the cost against Harrowgate Precast Inc.; the project manager revises the estimate by September 30.
Corliss Medical Group: suit to foreclose the lien filed August 12. Corliss has asked for mediation.
Resolved: a dividend of $150,000.00 to the shareholders, to be paid September 25.
Brindlewood School District: the district denied the time extension on September 15. HCS will not contest; the $41,250.00 is final.
Tideflats Cold Storage: the revised estimate adds $1,196,000.00 of cost; the job still expects a profit.
Cinderbrook Bank: the line of credit matures March 31, 2027. The Controller is to ask the bank to renew it.

Corliss Medical Group: the settlement signed October 8 is ratified: Corliss pays $110,000.00 by October 30, 2026 in full settlement of the $186,935.00 final billing, and HCS releases its lien on payment.
Line of credit: the $500,000.00 advance of October 9 is ratified. The line is $3,500,000.00 drawn of $4,000,000.00.
Cinderbrook Bank: the commitment letter of October 16 to renew the line to March 31, 2029 is accepted. Resolved: no dividends to the shareholders until the renewal closes.
The draft FY2026 financial statements and notes were reviewed. The Controller is to send them to the audit team for the report.
